title: Adventure outline
description: Repeated matched comparisons of TTRPG adventure outlines with and without explicit Dungeon Master skill invocation.

cases.title: Open adventure outline
cases.task: create an outline for TTRPG adventure

cases.title: Mountain caravan
cases.task: Create an outline for a fantasy TTRPG adventure for four new players and one three-hour session. The party has already agreed to escort a caravan across a dangerous mountain pass. Include the possibility of a straightforward combat encounter.

cases.title: Orbital salvage
cases.task: Create an outline for a science-fiction TTRPG adventure lasting two sessions. The characters are a salvage crew investigating an apparently abandoned orbital facility. Keep it system-neutral.

cases.title: Neighborhood celebration
cases.task: Create an outline for a contemporary TTRPG adventure for one evening of quiet, nonviolent play. The characters are preparing a neighborhood celebration while a disagreement threatens the event.

cases.title: Weather station horror
cases.task: Create an outline for a one-session horror TTRPG adventure at an isolated weather station. A tragic ending is acceptable. Use no established fictional setting.

cases.title: Mechanical structure
cases.task: Create an outline for a system-neutral exploration and puzzle TTRPG adventure for one session. It takes place inside an ancient mechanical structure and requires no combat.

anchors.0: The central situation cannot function as described, or major contradictions prevent play.
anchors.1: Severe deficiencies; substantial invention or repair required.
anchors.2: Partially effective, with an important identifiable weakness.
anchors.3: Motivations, events, and possible developments fit together, with ordinary preparation needed.
anchors.4: Strong, with only minor limitations between competent and exceptional.
anchors.5: The relationships between causes, actions, and consequences are especially convincing and productive for play.

dimensions.title: Opportunities for play and consequential action
dimensions.criterion: Opportunities for play and consequential action

anchors.0: Predetermined narration leaves players essentially nothing to do.
anchors.1: Severe deficiencies; substantial invention or repair required.
anchors.2: Partially effective, with an important identifiable weakness.
anchors.3: Players have concrete activities and can affect approaches, local outcomes, relationships, discoveries, or the ending.
anchors.4: Strong, with only minor limitations between competent and exceptional.
anchors.5: The material supports several compelling forms of engagement, and player actions produce intelligible, consequential differences.

anchors.0: No discernible adventure outline, or material is too confused to develop.
anchors.1: Severe deficiencies; substantial invention or repair required.
anchors.2: Partially effective, with an important identifiable weakness.
anchors.3: A GM can identify the starting situation, likely play, and a workable progression or organizing structure. Scope fits stated constraints.
anchors.4: Strong, with only minor limitations between competent and exceptional.
anchors.5: Preparation priorities and connections are immediately clear; the outline supplies unusually useful scaffolding without distracting excess.

anchors.0: Almost entirely interchangeable abstractions or disconnected ornament.
anchors.1: Severe deficiencies; substantial invention or repair required.
anchors.2: Partially effective, with an important identifiable weakness.
anchors.3: Concrete details establish an identifiable atmosphere and give the adventure some memorable material.
anchors.4: Strong, with only minor limitations between competent and exceptional.
anchors.5: Specific, evocative ideas work together and meaningfully shape what happens during play.

dimensions.title: Characters, opposition, and other active forces
dimensions.criterion: Characters, opposition, and other active forces

anchors.0: Central people or forces have no intelligible behavior, purpose, or effect on play.
anchors.1: Severe deficiencies; substantial invention or repair required.
anchors.2: Partially effective, with an important identifiable weakness.
anchors.3: Relevant people, institutions, creatures, environments, or other forces provide understandable pressures and interaction.
anchors.4: Strong, with only minor limitations between competent and exceptional.
anchors.5: Their behavior and relationships create especially compelling situations that a GM can develop or respond through.

anchors.0: Essential context or information is missing in a way that makes the intended activity unworkable.
anchors.1: Severe deficiencies; substantial invention or repair required.
anchors.2: Partially effective, with an important identifiable weakness.
anchors.3: The outline establishes participation and provides sufficient context, discoveries, or guidance for its intended activities.
anchors.4: Strong, with only minor limitations between competent and exceptional.
anchors.5: Setup and information are integrated especially well: players can engage, discoveries matter, and the GM can handle relevant uncertainty.

scoring.aggregation: Equal dimension mean across two independent paired-context judges; primary and transfer results reported separately.

judging.assessments: Score each candidate with evidence before direct A/B/tie preference; both candidates visible throughout.

limitations: Six hand-selected prompts and sixteen matched generation pairs do not support universal claims about TTRPG design.
Two judges use the same model family and ultra runtime as contestants; shared-model and style bias remain. No human calibration or cross-provider judge.
Dimension assessments are made within a blinded paired context, not separate individual presentations.
No answer-length control; explicit invocation includes context overhead and changed tool behavior.
Ultra may use runtime-internal collaboration; CLI session counts are not verified underlying model-agent counts.
Model and effort are exact CLI requests unless provider evidence positively attributes them.
